cli.autoids.hint: Change: mkey devices auto-ids <mode>. Names already given keep working.
cli.autoids.long:
Some devices have buttons without a standard name (for example, «Calculator» on a keyboard
or the buttons of an unusual joystick). mKey gives such a device the name UnKey (UnKey2, UnKey3…),
and its buttons numbers: in macros they are written {UnKey001}, {UnKey2.001}.
The names are kept in devices.yaml (mkey paths) and do not change after reconnecting.

Without a mode — show the current one; with a mode — change it:
  mkey devices auto-ids
  mkey devices auto-ids all
cli.autoids.mode.all: all devices with unnamed buttons, including service ones
cli.autoids.mode.smart: all devices with unnamed buttons except service ones (power, sleep, brightness)
cli.autoids.mode.unusual: only unusual devices (not a keyboard, mouse or gamepad)
cli.autoids.short: Which devices get automatic names (UnKey) for buttons without a name

cli.hotkeys.long:
Show and change mKey's own combinations. A combination is written by holding: ^{LCtrl}^{RAlt}{Space} — left Ctrl and right Alt held, Space pressed.

Examples:
  mkey hotkeys                                          show
  mkey hotkeys set record "^{Ctrl}^{Alt}{R}"             start/stop recording
  mkey hotkeys set record off                           turn the recording combination off
  mkey hotkeys set emergency "^{Esc}^{Backspace}{Enter}" emergency stop

Changes apply at once and are saved in the settings.

cli.inspect.long:
Shows the details of one input device: what its buttons are called in macros,
which axes it has and their ranges, the permanent device names (they do not change
after reconnecting). Buttons without an mKey name are listed separately with kernel names.

The device is given the same way as in the mkey devices list:
  mkey devices inspect event6          by file name
  mkey devices inspect logitech        by part of the name (if only one device matches)
  mkey devices inspect /dev/input/event6

All of them are plain text, you can open them in any text editor.
The ~ sign means your home folder.

cli.play.long:
Replays recorded keyboard, mouse, gamepad and touchscreen actions through mKey's virtual devices.
Stop: Ctrl+C here or Esc + Backspace + Enter together.

Examples:
  mkey play game                   once, as recorded
  mkey play game --speed 2         twice as fast
  mkey play game --repeat 10       10 times in a row
  mkey play game --loop            repeat until stopped
  mkey play game --pause 200       exactly 0.2 s between actions
  mkey play game --no-moves        without mouse moves

cli.rec.convert.long:
Creates a disabled project «From recording «name»» with a «Replay» event: presses, pauses, clicks and mouse moves become ordinary blocks you can edit in the window and run with a hotkey.

Examples:
  mkey rec convert game                  asks whether to simplify mouse moves
  mkey rec convert game --simplify       simplify: fewer blocks, almost the same path
  mkey rec convert game --no-simplify    every move is a separate block

cli.rec.long:
Records everything you do with the keyboard and mouse (for example, in a game) into a recording.
Stop recording: left Ctrl + right Alt + Space in any program (changeable in Settings) or Ctrl+C in this terminal.
Replay: mkey play <name>. Recording files are in the folder shown by mkey rec list.

Examples:
  mkey rec game          record as "game"
  mkey rec               name is mKeyRec_DDMMYYYY_HHMMSS (date and time)
  mkey rec list          list recordings and the folder they are in

cli.rename.long:
Gives a device or its button (axis) a clear name for macros. Old names (UnKey,
{UnKey001}) keep working, so existing macros do not break.

Name: letters, digits and «_», starting with a letter; case does not matter.
The device is given by its auto name (UnKey), name, eventN or part of its title;
the button — by its number (001, Axis01) or current name. mkey devices inspect shows the numbers.

Examples:
  mkey devices rename UnKey Sega                    device UnKey → Sega
  mkey devices rename Sega Start --button 001       button 001 → {Sega.Start}
  mkey devices rename Sega --clear                  remove the name (UnKey stays)

cli.root.long:
mKey presses keys and buttons for you — on hotkeys, timers, typed words and other events — records and replays keyboard and mouse actions, and creates virtual gamepads and other input devices.

Run "mkey gui" to open the web interface, or "mkey help <command>" for help on a command.
Where settings, projects and recordings are kept: mkey paths
cli.root.long.cli:
mKey records and replays keyboard and mouse actions, reacts to hotkeys and runs macros.

Help for a command: mkey help <command>. Record and replay: mkey rec <name>, mkey play <name>.
Where settings, projects and recordings are kept: mkey paths
cli.root.short: Keyboard and mouse macros for Linux

cli.send.long:
Run a macro written in the mKey language.

Examples:
  mkey send '{Enter}'                          press Enter
  mkey send '^{Ctrl}{C}~{Ctrl}'                copy (Ctrl+C)
  mkey send '{"Hello!"}'                       type text
  mkey send '^{Shift}{"Hello, Vera!"}~{Shift}'  type in capitals
  mkey send --delay 3s '{"Hello"}'             wait 3 seconds, then type

The macro runs in the currently active window. Syntax: docs/dsl.md.

cli.update.ask: Install version {version} now? mKey will restart
cli.update.flag.auto: check once a day: on or off
cli.update.long:
Checks whether a new version is out and (with your consent) installs it: downloads, verifies the checksum, replaces the program and restarts mKey. The previous version stays next to it (mkey.old).

Examples:
  mkey update             check and offer to install
  mkey update --check     only check
  mkey update --auto on   check once a day (off — do not check)
cli.update.short: Check for and install a new mKey version
cli.var.no_project: specify the project: --project name (inside mKey scripts it is set automatically)
cli.virtual.long:
Virtual devices are described in a project (the virtual_devices section) and exist while
the project is enabled. For example, an Xbox 360 gamepad «pad2»:

  virtual_devices:
    - { name: pad2, template: xbox360 }

In macros: {pad2.South} — press button A, {pad2.LX=-1} — stick fully left.
Games see such a device as a real gamepad.
cli.virtual.none: No virtual devices: no enabled project describes them (help: mkey devices virtual --help).

cli.watch.long:
Continuously shows which keys and buttons are pressed and on which device, with their macro names ({Mouse0}, {A}, {South}…). Presses are saved to a file only with --out.

Examples:
  mkey devices watch                      keys, buttons, wheel and axes
  mkey devices watch --moves              plus mouse movements
  mkey devices watch --device Logitech    only devices with "Logitech" in the name
  mkey devices watch --out log.txt        and save the log to a file

dsl.already_held: the key {key} is already held — it cannot be held or pressed again before ~{{key}}
dsl.axis_as_key: «{name}» is an axis: it is not pressed but set to a position, for example {{name}=0.5}
dsl.axis_chord: an axis value applies to a single axis, without repeat or hold
dsl.axis_expected: «{name}» is not an axis: a position (=…) is set only for axes, for example {pad2.LX=0.5}
dsl.bad_duration: invalid duration "{text}": use milliseconds (250) or seconds (1.5s)
dsl.bad_hotkey: write a combination by holding: ^{Ctrl}^{Alt}{H} (held keys and the last one pressed) or a single key: {F8}
dsl.bad_repeat: the repeat count must be between 1 and {max}
dsl.binding_option: setting «{option}» does not fit binding «{name}». Which settings fit which bindings — see the projects help (section «Axis bindings»)
dsl.binding_range: binding «{name}»: setting «{option}» must be from {min} to {max}
dsl.binding_threshold: binding «{name}» needs threshold — how far to tilt to press the button, from −1 to 1, not 0 (e.g. 0.5 — half right/down, −0.5 — left/up; for the mouse the sign is the direction)
dsl.binding_value: for the axis «{name}» set a position value from −1 to 1 (for example, −1 — fully left), except 0
dsl.brace_key: there is no "{char}" key — it is Shift with [ or ]. To type the character: {"{char}"}; to press the key: {LBracket} or {RBracket}
dsl.cannot_send: mKey cannot press the button {key} ({kernel}) yet — it can be caught in hotkeys and conditions
dsl.chord_in_braces: braces hold one key, but here is a combination "{keys}". In a macro write it by holding: {macro}; in a hotkey: {hotkey}
dsl.empty_braces: empty braces {} — specify a key, e.g. {Enter}
dsl.many_touchscreens: there are several touchscreens ({list}) — name the one to touch: {Touch name 50% 80%}
dsl.no_touchscreen: no virtual touchscreen — add one to an enabled project: virtual_devices: [{ name: screen, template: touchscreen }]
dsl.not_held: the key {key} was not held — ~{{key}} needs ^{{key}} before it
dsl.not_supported: this feature is not supported yet ({what}) and will come in a later version
dsl.not_touchscreen: «{device}» is not a touchscreen (template touchscreen is needed)
dsl.pause_range: in a random pause [a..b] the first number must not exceed the second
dsl.prefix_not_allowed: ^ (press) and ~ (release) can only be used with keys, without repeat or hold
dsl.repeat_and_hold: repeat (*N) and hold cannot be combined
dsl.screen_unknown: the screen size is unknown, so a point in pixels cannot be converted — use percent ({Touch 50% 80%}) or set the size in config.yaml: modules.desktop.screen: "1920x1080"
dsl.star_only_release: {*} can only be used as ~{*} — "release everything"
dsl.text_outside: character "{char}" outside braces. To type text, put it in {"..."}
dsl.too_long: pause or hold is too long: at most {max}
dsl.unclosed_group: missing closing parenthesis ")" of a group
dsl.unclosed_pause: missing closing bracket "]" of a pause
dsl.unclosed_text: the text is missing its closing quote "
dsl.unknown_button: device «{device}» has no button «{button}» (mkey devices inspect shows its numbers and names)
dsl.untypeable_char: character "{char}" cannot be typed with layouts: {layouts}
notify.emergency.body: All macros stopped, the keyboard is released. Hotkeys and events are paused — resume: mkey resume
notify.emergency.title: mKey: emergency stop
notify.project_error.body: The previous version of the project keeps running. Error: {error}
notify.project_error.title: mKey: error in project "{project}"
notify.setup_needed.body: Not everything is ready (for example, no keyboard access). Open a terminal and run: mkey doctor --fix
notify.setup_needed.title: mKey: setup needed
place.config.description: The config.yaml file: all program settings by section, each with an explanation. Plain text, you can edit it in any text editor (takes effect after mKey restarts).
place.devices.description: The devices.yaml file: automatic device names (UnKey) and numbers of their unnamed buttons. Kept by mKey.
place.log.description: The mKey work log: useful when something goes wrong. Pressed keys are never written to it.
place.plugins.description: Installed plugins: each folder holds plugin.yaml and the plugin files.
place.projects.description: Project files *.mkey.yaml: events, hotkeys, macros. New and changed files are picked up right away.
place.recordings.description: Action recordings *.mkrec — plain text, one line per action. You can delete unwanted lines in any text editor.
platform.device_access.mdev: mdev rules and the input group
platform.device_access.uaccess: udev rule for the active session (uaccess)
platform.elevate.press_enter: Done. Press Enter to close this window.
platform.elevate.prompt: mKey: to grant access to input devices, enter the administrator password.
platform.elevator.terminal-doas: doas in a new terminal window
platform.elevator.terminal-sudo: sudo in a new terminal window
plugins.failed: Plugin «{plugin}» is turned off: it crashed three times in a minute ({error}). Turn it on again in Plugins in the mKey window.
project.problem.no_trigger: it is not set when to run
rec.problem.action: unclear action «{arg}» (possible: ^{A} — press, ~{A} — release, move, wheel, hwheel, ev)
rec.problem.caps: the caps line is malformed or refers to a device not listed above («{arg}») — better not edit it
rec.problem.created: the date is written incorrectly (example: created 2026-10-01T12:00:00Z)
rec.problem.device: the device line does not match the pattern (example: device 0 mouse "Name")
rec.problem.device_number: the device number must be a number, but it says «{arg}»
rec.problem.header: the first line must be «mkrec 1», but the file has «{arg}»
rec.problem.key: unknown key «{arg}» (names are the same as in macros: A, Enter, LShift, Mouse0…)
rec.problem.line: unclear start of the line «{arg}»: an action line starts with the time in seconds, for example 1.250
rec.problem.negative: after the shift lines the time became less than zero ({arg} s) — reduce the shift above
rec.problem.numbers: «{arg}» is missing numbers or a number is written incorrectly
rec.problem.old_format: this is a recording from the first mKey version in the old format and cannot be read — please record it again
rec.problem.pointer: pointer must be followed by center
rec.problem.read: the file could not be read: {arg}
rec.problem.shift: shift must be followed by a number of seconds, for example shift -2.5 (earlier) or shift 1 (later), but it says «{arg}»
rec.problem.short: the time must be followed by a device number and actions, for example: 1.250 0 ^{A}
rec.problem.version: the recording was made by a newer mKey version (format {arg}) — please update mKey
setup.check.elevator.manual: mKey cannot request administrator rights itself — you will need to run a command manually
setup.check.elevator.ok: Administrator rights will be requested via {method}
setup.check.input.denied: No access to input devices (0 of {total}) — mKey cannot see key presses
setup.check.input.ok: All input devices are accessible ({readable} of {total}) — mKey can see key presses
setup.check.input.partial: Only some input devices are accessible ({readable} of {total})
setup.check.kernel.old: Linux kernel {version} is too old: 5.4 or newer is required
setup.check.kernel.unknown: Could not determine the kernel version: {error}
setup.check.rules.missing: mKey access rules are not installed (suitable method: {method})
setup.check.rules.unsupported: There is no automatic way to grant device access on this system
setup.check.runtime_dir.fallback: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR is not set, using fallback directory {dir}
setup.check.session.none: No graphical session found ({type}) — windows and screen features will be unavailable
setup.check.uinput.denied: No access to virtual input (/dev/uinput) — mKey cannot press keys
setup.check.uinput.missing: The uinput virtual input module is not loaded — mKey cannot press keys
setup.check.uinput.ok: Virtual input (uinput) is available — mKey can press keys

template.capslock_esc.description: The CapsLock key works as Esc.
template.capslock_esc.name: CapsLock as Esc
template.hold_mouse.description: Ctrl+Alt+H holds the left mouse button for 1.5 seconds.
template.hold_mouse.name: Hold mouse button
template.replay.description: F9 replays a recording — put the name of your recording into the "Play a recording" block.

template.text_shortcut.description: Type "btw" and a space to get "by the way".
template.text_shortcut.name: Text shortcuts
tray.play_soon: Replaying «{name}» in {seconds} s — switch to the window you need. Stop: Esc + Backspace + Enter.
tray.project_invalid: mKey: project «{project}» has an error — it was not enabled
tray.recording_saved: Recording «{name}» saved. Replay it from the icon menu: «Replay recording».
tray.recording_started: Recording started. Stop it from the mKey icon menu.
tray.recording_started_hotkey: Recording started. Stop it with {hotkey} in any program or from the mKey icon menu.
tray.tooltip.active: Running. Emergency stop: Esc + Backspace + Enter
trigger.device.description: A keyboard, mouse or gamepad is connected or disconnected.
trigger.hotkey.description: A key combination or a mouse/gamepad button.
trigger.hotkey.field.consume: Don't pass the press to programs
trigger.hotkey.field.consume.hint: Programs will not see this press — only mKey will.
trigger.hotkey.field.on.toggle: press turns on, next press turns off
trigger.hotstring.description: Fires after a typed word followed by a space or Enter.
trigger.hotstring.field.replace.hint: If set, the typed word is erased and this text is typed.
trigger.manual.description: Started with the "Run" button, from the mKey icon menu or by another event.
trigger.sequence: When I press keys one after another…
trigger.sequence.description: A sequence of presses, e.g. G then G.
trigger.startup.description: Once when mKey starts or the project is enabled.
trigger.timer.description: Periodically or once after a delay.
update.available: A new mKey version {version} is out. Update: Settings → Updates or mkey update.
update.reason.dev: this is a developer build without a version number
update.reason.package: it is installed by a package — update it with your system's package manager
vdev.template.custom.description: Your own set of buttons and axes: buttons and axes in the project.
vdev.template.ds4.description: Like a DualShock 4: the same buttons and axes as Xbox, triggers both as buttons and axes, rumble.
vdev.template.joystick.description: A generic joystick: 12 buttons, 6 axes and a hat switch.
vdev.template.keyboard.description: One more keyboard (for example, for a second player).
vdev.template.touchscreen.description: A 10-touch touchscreen (touches from macros will come later).
vdev.template.xbox360.description: Games see it as a wired Xbox 360 gamepad: South/East/West/North (A/B/X/Y), LB/RB, LT/RT triggers, LX/LY/RX/RY sticks, D-pad, rumble.
